title: kv-cache-seqlen-edgecase-debug-notes
content:
Goal: capture quick repro steps, logs, and hypotheses for the seqlen>4096 KV-cache + attention-kernel edge case. Notes are messy - primer for pair-debug with Ethan/Maya.

Symptoms observed:
- Intermittent incorrect generation when sequence length grows past ~4096 tokens during long-context workloads. Outputs contain repeated phrases or token corruption after a certain prefix.
- In some runs we get a crash (segfault) inside attention kernel; in others the model runs but outputs are garbage after the boundary.
- Behavior correlated with kernel fallback: when runtime selects fused_attention_v2 we often see issues; generic_attention seems safe but slower.

Immediate repro (minimal):
1) python repro/repro_seqlen_kv.py --model llama-13b --seq-len 8192 --batch 1 --prompt-file tests/long_prompt.txt
2) OR run locally with docker image: docker run --rm -e MODEL=llama-13b redwood/serving:local-debug /bin/bash -c "./serve --max-seq 8192 --kernel auto --load-model /models/llama-13b"
3) curl test: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -d '{"model":"llama-13b","input":"<long prompt>", "max_tokens": 4000}'

Key log snippets (from /var/log/serving/runtime.log):
[2026-02-24 14:12:05] INFO Selected kernel: fused_attention_v2 (SM75, autotuned)
[2026-02-24 14:12:05] WARN KV cache resize: expanding kv buffer (old=4096 new=8192)
[2026-02-24 14:12:05] ERROR attention_kernel.cpp:243 invalid KV index computed for head=3 idx=8191 (max_valid=4095)
[2026-02-24 14:12:05] FATAL segmentation fault at 0x7ffc...

Variant run where it doesn't crash but output corrupted:
[2026-02-26 09:03:11] INFO Selected kernel: fused_attention_v2 (autotuned)
[2026-02-26 09:03:12] INFO Fallback policy: retrying with generic_attention for current batch
[2026-02-26 09:03:12] INFO Generated 4096 tokens OK; continuing...
[2026-02-26 09:03:22] WARN Attention mask mismatch: kv_len=8192 mask_len=4096 -> zeroing suffix

Immediate hypotheses:
- KV cache resize path has stale index math when switching from a lower max_seq to a higher max_seq at runtime. Possibly off-by-one in modular indexing or pointer arithmetic when copying old cache into new larger buffer.
- fused_attention_v2 contains vectorized index math optimized for power-of-two layouts; when buffer growth uses non power-of-two sizes we hit invalid index calculations.
- Autotuner selects fused kernel based on perf profile from shorter sequences; kernel not robust to buffer growth mid-run. Generic kernel is safer because it uses scalar index math.
- Race between request thread and cache-resize: a request may be reading kv pointers while the resize/copy is happening -> intermittent corruption vs deterministic crash.

Commands/experiments tried so far (with quick notes):
- Repro with --kernel=generic -> no crash, correct outputs (slow).
- Repro with --kernel=fused_attention_v2 and --force-resize=preallocate -> no crash (preallocate avoids resize path).
- Added logging around KV resize; saw expected copy but noticed old_tail index used instead of old_head in one branch (suspicious).
- Instrumented memcpy to fill pre-copy region with 0xAA and post-copy with 0x55 to detect overlap; overlap observed only when batch_size>1 and when we took the resize path between batches.
- Added a crude lock around resize -> removes crashes in local runs but perf regression.

Short-term mitigations to deploy to staging: (notes for ops)
- Force kernel selection to generic_attention for seqlen > 4096 until root cause fixed. (runtime flag: --prefer-kernel=generic-for-long-seq)
- Preallocate KV caches for sessions that opt-in to long-context (config: session.max_seq_reserved = 8192).

Next debugging steps (todo):
- [ ] Write unit test for kv_resize() that simulates interleaved readers (use tsan if possible).
- [ ] Audit index calculations in fused_attention_v2 kernels: check modular arithmetic when base index >= old_capacity.
- [ ] Reproduce in a deterministic harness: run single-threaded but force interleaved read via yield points (insert test hooks in code).
- [ ] Try compiled kernels with sanitizers (ASAN/UBSAN) to catch invalid memory accesses.
- [ ] Evaluate whether kernel autotuner should include a robustness score (prefer stable kernel for long-seq workloads).

Notes-to-self on where code likely is: 
- kv cache code: runtime/kv_cache.cpp (resize(), read_index())
- fused kernel: kernels/fused_attention_v2.cu (indexing helpers at top)
- autotuner: runtime/kernel_autotuner.cpp

Reproducer quick script pointers: 
- repro/repro_seqlen_kv.py - small python loop that toggles max_seq at runtime
- tests/long_prompt.txt - 6k token lorem-ish prompt used in testing

Random breadcrumbs (from slack/dev threads):
- @ethan: "saw similar pattern last quarter, fixed by adding fence before memcpy in resize path"
- @maya: "I remember an issue where AVX512 kernels assumed 64-byte alignment; unaligned resize led to UBs"

If we need to ship a hotfix: consider conservative approach: 1) Force generic kernel for seqlen>threshold 2) preallocate/reserve kv buffers on session creation 3) add a quick lock around resize. Then follow up with a proper concurrency-safe resize and kernel fix.

Long-term: make autotuner aware of session-level constraints (min-max seq) and prefer kernels that support dynamic growth, or change resize to use copy-into-new-buffer-then-atomic-swap with proper barriers.

Patch notes ideas for PR: small change to kv_cache.cpp to ensure old_head/old_tail semantics; add unit test; update autotuner to mark fused_attention_v2 as "not safe for dynamic-growth" until proven.

Open questions to triage with team: 
- Are there any other kernels with similar index math assumptions? (ask kernels owners)
- Are we comfortable shipping a lock-based mitigation in Dedicated? Perf impact measurements needed.
- How frequent are long-context sessions in prod (need telemetry query)?

Quick perf/regression local numbers (informal): 
- generic kernel (no resize): baseline 100ms per 256 tokens
- fused_attention_v2 (no resize): ~35ms per 256 tokens
- fused_attention_v2 with resize+lock: ~80ms per 256 tokens

Links to reproduce infra: 
- Local docker image tag: redwood/serving:kv-debug-20260224
- Git branch: debug/kv-resize-seqlen

End of notes. Will clean into a proper bug report once we have a deterministic repro.
